How we work with you

  • Scope in writing first

    Projects and repairs start with a written scope and quote that you approve before work begins.

  • Your permission, every session

    Remote sessions only start when you let us in. We never ask for your passwords.

  • Updates in plain language

    You will always know what stage your project, ticket, or repair is at, and what happens next.

  • Support after launch

    Maintenance and support options keep your website and devices working after the handover.

Three divisions, one team that answers for all of it

Most small organizations need a website, someone to call when a computer misbehaves, and a fix when hardware fails. Jemawe covers all three so you are not managing three vendors.

Why organizations choose Jemawe

We are a small team, and that is the point: the people who scope your work are the people who build and support it.

About Jemawe

Practical recommendations

We suggest what fits your budget and goals, including when a simpler option will do.

Reliable communication

Clear updates at each stage and straight answers when something changes.

Built around your customers

We design for the people who use your site or tool every day.

Support that continues

Maintenance and IT support keep things working long after launch day.

Modern, maintainable code

Current tools chosen for the size of the job, documented for whoever comes next.

A transparent process

Written scope, visible milestones, and no surprise requirements halfway through.

How a project moves from idea to launch

The same four stages apply whether you need a five-page website or a custom application. You approve each stage before the next begins.

  1. Consultation

    We learn what you need, who it is for, and what success looks like.

  2. Planning

    A written scope, sitemap or feature list, timeline, and quote for your approval.

  3. Development

    We design, build, and test, sharing progress so you can give feedback early.

  4. Launch and support

    We launch together, hand over what you need, and stay available for support.

See the full development process

Common questions

Short answers to what people ask before getting in touch.

Read all FAQs
How much does a website cost?

It depends on the number of pages, features, and content you need. After a short consultation we send a written quote, so you know the cost before anything starts.

Do you offer support 24 hours a day?

No. Remote IT support is scheduled. When you submit a request, we confirm a session time with you directly.

Will you ask for my computer password?

No. Our forms never ask for passwords, and a remote session starts only when you approve it on your own screen.

Can you work on a website someone else built?

Often, yes. We review the site first and tell you plainly whether maintaining, improving, or rebuilding it makes the most sense.

Tell us what you are working on

Share a few details about your project, problem, or device. We will reply with next steps and, where it applies, a written quote.
